extracted.intended_audience: administrative law practitioners, policymakers, agency staff, and public stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the official procedural steps and standards ACUS follows to produce Recommendations and occasional Statements: selecting/engaging researchers, preparing comprehensive reports, committee drafting, Council/Assembly approval, and implementation. Also explains Statements as an alternative, non‑recommendation output of the same process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function — bring together public and private sectors to recommend improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose statement establishing that ACUS's core role is convening public and private stakeholders to identify and recommend reforms to administrative and regulatory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement of consultants with Council approval
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process requirement: consultant engagements must be authorized by the Office of the Chairman and approved by the Council; consultants (or in-house staff) perform the investigative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in-house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive standard: recommendations should be grounded in a comprehensive research report produced by the engaged consultants or in-house staff; implies evidence‑based, documentable analysis as the basis for any recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion and drafting of a Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council and, with approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberative step: an internal committee reviews the research report and is responsible for converting findings into a draft Recommendation for higher‑level review and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council approval and Assembly adoption following debate
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft Recommendation is submitted to the Council and, with Council approval, to the Assembly; following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance and approval criteria: recommendations require multi‑level approval — Council signoff and Assembly adoption after debate — indicating deliberation, consensus, and formal adoption procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation responsibility for adopted Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation, ACUS undertakes to implement it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accountability requirement: adoption carries an obligation for ACUS to pursue implementation of the Recommendation, not merely to publish it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and character of 'Statements' as non‑recommendation outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a 'Statement' to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative output standard: Statements are typically produced by the same process that leads to recommendations but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than prescriptive recommendations; ACUS has adopted 19 such statements (included in the searchable database).
